moments.quote: Each one was occupied by three bodies of human shape but only 3 feet tall, dressed in metallic cloth of a very fine texture.
moments.short: Each one was occupied by three bodies of human shape but only 3 feet tall…

moments.alt: Infrared targeting-pod view: a small white oblong held in the pod's brackets slides out to the left edge of the frame at about 74-75 s and is gone.

moments.quote: Mr. Gerald Anderson, an alleged witness of events at the site 175 miles northwest of Roswell, recalled, “I thought they were plastic dolls.”
moments.short: Mr. Gerald Anderson, … recalled, “I thought they were plastic dolls.”

moments.alt: Infrared view above the clouds: the dark object in the targeting brackets turns from tilted to level at about 29-30 s, then tilts again.

moments.quote: We were able to identify one reported UAP with high confidence. In that case, we identified the object as a large, deflating balloon. The others remain unexplained.
moments.short: In that case, we identified the object as a large, deflating balloon. The others remain unexplained.

moments.alt: Close-up of the Department of War's enlarged inset of the lunar sky: three faint dots of light in a small triangle, two bluish and one paler, almost white.
Infrared view of the ocean surface: the pod's cursor box searches the waves, captures a small white object at about 12 s and locks on as a range readout appears.
Gemini VII air-to-ground audio: Houston asks whether the bogey Frank Borman reported is the booster or an actual sighting; after a 'say again', the crew's reply ends 'actual sighting'.

notes: Skeptic pass (2026-11-09), all checked against page images and frames. Gemini 7 audio: timed with a local whisper transcript of the hosted audio (speech energy matches): 'Bogey at ten o'clock high' 63.8-65.3 s; Houston 'say again, seven' 72.7-74.6 s; 'Said we have a bogey at ten o'clock high' 75.8-77.7 s; 'Roger' 79.2 s; near-silence 80-92 s; Houston 'Is that the booster or is that an actual sighting?' 92.0-96.0 s; Houston 'Say again, seven' 100-101 s; crew answer ending 'actual sighting' 102-105.2 s; then 'estimate distance or size?' 107-111 s, 'We also have the booster in sight' 112-114 s, 'hundreds of little particles' 118-125.7 s. The window moved from 84-98 (opened on 8 s of hiss) to 91.5-106: the question and the answer. The crew answer's middle words are unclear by machine transcript, so the alt does not quote them. FLIR1: exact-time frames show the object still in the brackets at 74.13 s, just left of them at 74.40 s, at the left edge 74.67-74.93 s, gone by 75.20 s (video ends 76.2 s). Gimbal (new): rotation verified on frames 25-32 s; tilted at 26 s, level at 29-30 s, tilted the other way by 31 s. GoFast (new): exact-time frames show the cursor box resizing over the waves 10-11.3 s, closing on a small white dot 11.7-12.0 s, lock with '4.4 RNG' at 12.3 s. Roswell short drops the appositive 'an alleged witness of events at the site 175 miles northwest of Roswell,' (cut at its commas); the quote keeps it. Printed page number on PDF p.25 is 14; footnote 12 follows the quote and is excluded. ODNI short starts at a sentence start ('In that case,') and is exactly 100 characters; the quote adds the preceding sentence. Lens box now stops before the period after 'balloon'. Hottel short ends at the comma after 'tall'; the line box includes 'tall,'. Lens 'three bodies of human shape' breaks across two printed lines, so the lens is 'occupied by three bodies' on one line. Faces exceed 60% width on purpose so no printed word is cut at the edges: Hottel 0.69 (typed lines run 0.17-0.835; the old 0.19-0.835 box cut the first letters of every line), Roswell 0.627 (text runs to 0.68; the old box cut 'based', 'aliens.', 'Mr.' at the right and the top line), ODNI 0.80 (lines run 0.118-0.881; the old 0.775 right edge cut 'The others' off the moment line). Roswell's quote sits near the page bottom, so its face runs from the 'Careful examination' paragraph to the end of the paragraph with the quote. Apollo square tightened to 140x140 px of full.webp around the three dots inside the Department of War inset (the dots shown are the inset's enlargement, not the tiny original spot); at 120 px the dots read about 1.4x larger than with the old 200 px square. The lower dot is pale, near-neutral grey (not orange), so the alt now says so.
